title: ToggleButton
lead: A toggle button is a button that can be checked on and off.

examples.name: Shape
examples.description: A toggle button can be rounded, circular, or square.

examples.name: Appearance
examples.description:
- `(undefined)`: the toggle button appears with the default style
- `primary`: emphasizes the toggle button as a primary action.
- `outline`: removes background styling.
- `subtle`: minimizes emphasis to blend into the background until hovered or focused
- `transparent`: removes background and border styling.

examples.name: Accessible Appearance
examples.description:
Appearance variants with isAccessible set, showing more contrasting colors when checked. The primary variant uses the same colors, but with an inset stroke for the checked state.

This approach is available for when the icon is not used to differentiate checked vs. unchecked states.

examples.name: Icon
examples.description: The ToggleButton has an `icon` slot that, if specified, renders an icon either `before` or `after` the children, as specified by the `iconPosition` prop.

examples.name: Size
examples.description: A toggle button supports `small`, `medium` and `large` size. Default size is `medium`.

examples.name: Disabled
examples.description:
A toggle button can be `disabled` or `disabledFocusable`.
              `disabledFocusable` is used in scenarios where it is important to keep a consistent tab order
              for screen reader and keyboard users. The primary example of this pattern is when
              the disabled toggle button is in a menu or a commandbar and is seldom used for standalone buttons.

examples.name: Checked
examples.description:
A toggle button can be checked or unchecked. Unchecked is default.
      If a checked value is given, the button is 'controlled' and will only change state when the
      props value changes.

examples.name: With Long Text
examples.description: Text wraps after it hits the max width of the component.
